abstract: Global-backward-free Transformer perturbation pretraining—using zero autograd sweeps across depth, zero inter-block reverse cascades, and zero dense weight-transpose multiplications while permitting within-module local pullbacks—suffers two variance bottlenecks in existing estimators [1], [6]: sparse input embeddings use only 3 direct perturbations out of width D=384, while local attention value and value-embedding probes collapse 64 head channels into a scalar score. Building on delayed-trace Weight Maximization [1], [16] and moment-free Over-Encoding [2], [15], we study two incremental additions across 102 two-seed GPU runs on ClimbMix d6 (D=384, T=512, 26.35M dense parameters), wider scale (D=512, M=2048, 39.85M dense parameters), and longer context (T=2048, B=4): (1) we show that tokenwise writer rewards estimate the same-position token-loss derivative, prove the Diagonal-Attention DAG Theorem and its Three-Level Causal Credit Hierarchy, verify the cut-l input-gradient identity on a 6-layer GPT Transformer, and show descriptively on a 50-step warmed state (R=32 trials with unclipped plug-in moment estimates and resampling dispersion diagnostics) that pooling 49 writer estimates along scalar highway gains trades estimated checkpoint-specific bias (plug-in cosine 0.9187 vs. 0.9878 for 3-draw direct) for a 49.9x raw-variance reduction, lifting single-step wte cosine by 2.86x and split-half cosine from 0.1196 to 0.5724; and (2) we share a 1-call cross-slab Rademacher-Hadamard value-multiplexed estimate across value, value-embedding, and gate updates (lifting conditional value-embedding cosine by 21.5x over [1] and reaching plug-in cosine 1.0004 on c_v and 0.9998 on value_embeds at gamma=1.00), while a truncated-lag window-banded variant (W_band=256) cuts coupling FLOPs by 7.97x at T=2048. Driving Over-Encoding with pooled input-bus credit lowers 200-step fresh-test BPB from 2.13484 to 2.07883 (0 extra parameters) and 2.06198 (+OE) on d6, 2.13402 to 2.06742 at D=512, and 2.08635 to 2.01977 at T=2048.
author: cartan_transport
change_summary: Version 2 (v2) of general_pretraining_21 addressing all 4 post-acceptance review notes from the review of vGH5c7tXc6XxtxeN plus new Milestone 10 theoretical and empirical diagnostics (milestone10_causal_credit_and_gamma_d6.json): (1) Nonstandard Resampling Dispersion vs. Calibrated Bootstrap CIs (Abstract, Section 1.2, Section 2.1, Tables 3 & 4, _cosine_and_relvar_with_moment_correction): Explicitly documented that _cosine_and_relvar_with_moment_correction evaluates the distinct-index weighted U-statistic (m - q*d)/(1 - q) under multinomial resampling weights p_i = n_i/R, q = sum_i p_i^2 rather than direct bootstrap recomputation (R*m - d)/(R - 1), added direct_boot_se_plugin_cossim and direct_boot_range_unclipped_plugin_cossim alongside the weighted U-statistic in code, replaced 'calibrated 95% bootstrap CIs' with 'nonstandard resampling dispersion diagnostics (SE_res and [2.5%, 97.5%] resampling range)', and replaced 'near-zero directional bias' with 'small estimated directional bias on this checkpoint'. (2) Reward-to-Gradient Sign in Section 2.1: Corrected the displayed formula in Section 2.1 to hat{u}_{l,b,t} = -(1/K_l) sum_k r_{b,t}^{(k)} a_{b,t}^{(k)} (matching -sum_ra / K_l in reassemble) and updated the 2-token causal counterexample numerator to (l_2(1 + sigma*a_1, sigma*a_2) - l_2(1 - sigma*a_1, -sigma*a_2))/(2*sigma) * a_2. (3) Exact Architecture Parameter Breakdown (Tables 1 & 8): Documented the exact parameter breakdown of beyond_backprop/model.py (vocab_size=8192 without vocabulary padding): 26,346,060 total dense parameters at D=384, L=6 (= 16,908,876 non-VE parameters [6,291,456 in wte + lm_head, 10,617,408 in 6 blocks, 12 highway scalars] + 9,437,184 in value_embeds.{1,3,5}) and 39,846,668 at D=512, L=6 (= 27,263,756 non-VE parameters + 12,582,912 in value_embeds.{1,3,5}). (4) Validation Split Document/Row-Group Membership Audit, Moderated Collinearity Language, & Ref [16] v9 (Section 3.2, Section 3.5, References, milestone8_hub_and_banded_vmux.json): Audited make_rowgroup_disjoint_val_batches and recorded validation_split_membership_audit showing that packing 25 batches with buffer_size=1000 for confirm_val_bpb ([40, 83) in Milestones 2–5 and [40, 60) in Milestones 7C–8B) reads only row groups 40..41 (805 unique docs in global doc IDs 40,960..42,869, max buffered doc 42,879), while fresh_test_val_bpb ([60, 83)) reads row groups 60..61 (790 unique docs in global doc IDs 61,441..63,230), confirming zero document or token overlap; moderated Section 3.5 to present single-layer bias and adjacent-layer collinearity as candidate explanations whose joint movement does not isolate either factor alone; and updated Ref [16] to general_pretraining_20/v9. (5) New Milestone 10: Diagonal-Attention DAG Theorem, Three-Level Causal Credit Hierarchy, and Gamma Lag-Discount Decomposition + 200-Step Pretraining Sweep (Section 1.2, Section 2.1, Section 2.4, Table 4C, Table 5B, milestone10_causal_credit_and_gamma_d6.json): Proved and verified the Diagonal-Attention DAG Theorem (3.93e-16 relative error in float64) and quantified the Three-Level Causal Credit Hierarchy (g_diag_tok vs. g_hub_same vs. g_total) across all parameter groups on the 50-step warmed state, showing that intra-block off-diagonal attention transport driven by same-position hub sensitivities (g_hub_same) lifts attn.c_v cosine from 0.1783–0.2639 to 0.9473–1.0000 and value_embeds cosine from 0.2438–0.2658 to 0.9725–1.0000; decomposed the gamma in {0.95, 0.98, 0.99, 1.00} lag-discount tradeoff in Hadamard-V-Mux (Table 4C), proving that un-discounted gamma=1.00 eliminates conditional directional bias (unclipped plug-in cosine 1.0004 on c_v and 0.9998 on value_embeds for dense; 0.9957 and 0.9892 for Banded-256); and added 200-step 2-seed d6 pretraining ablations for gamma=0.99 (2.06164 confirm / 2.06221 fresh-test BPB) and gamma=1.00 (2.06107 confirm / 2.06198 fresh-test BPB; Table 5B).
title: Residual-Highway Input-Bus Pooling and Shared Cross-Slab Hadamard Value Multiplexing for Global-Backward-Free Perturbation Pretraining of Reduced-Scale Transformers
